newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rise by lunch on foreign fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rise by lunch on foreign fund buying.

text.p: Thai stocks posted strong gains by the lunch break on Monday as foreign funds flowed into the heavily discounted Thai equity market, traders said.
The SET Index gained 21.15 points, or 4.40 percent, to 501.40 by the lunchbreak. The SET 50 rose 2.19 points, or 6.54 percent to 35.66 on trade worth a 3.14 billion baht.

"I think today's gains in part represent a reallocation of funds to Thailand by foreign investors with a long term, say two year, view of the market," said a trader at a Thai Military Bank affiliated broker.
The market is waiting to see how new Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya performs. The cabinet on Tuesday is due to approve decrees for revamping regulations for finance firms to merge, dealers said.
The central bank is due to release monthly economic data including foreign reserves on Thursday while the government is due to submit budget plans to parliament on Wednesday.
U.S. investment funds picked bank and communications stocks, brokers said. Bangkok Bank gained nine to 118, TelecomAsia added two to 28, Thai Farmers Bank put on 6.5 to 81.5. -- James Mclean
